newsitem.title: USA: Interprovincial says crude lines still running low rates.
newsitem.headline: Interprovincial says crude lines still running low rates.

text.p: Interprovincial Pipe Line Inc said Wednesday that crude lines affected by the power outage in northern Minnesota were still running at reduced rates after a brief increase overnight.

A number of lines have been hit since Saturday night when severe weather cut power to three northern Minnesota pumping stations on the lines, which initially took out about a million barrels per day (bpd) of the system's 1.4 million bpd.

"Overnight we were allowed to run some extra power by the power companies which achieved some extra rate for us both on Line two and Line three. We had hoped to get a major fix on extra power to a number of locations but that has not worked out to date...there appears to be a further problem," an IPL spokesman said.

Line one is still operating at fairly minimal levels, Line 2b is running at a rate of 2,000 cubic meters an hour (12,579 barrels/hour), and Line three, which had an increased flow rate for several hours overnight, was back to a rate of 3,000 cubic meters/hour (18,865 barrels/hour) early Wednesday, the spokesman said.
Line 2b runs from Edmonton, Alberta to Superior, Wisconsin carries light, medium and sythetic crudes plus condensate and has a usual flow rate of 18,869 barrels per hour.
Line 3 runs from Edmonton to Superior, carries light, medium, heavy and synthetic crudes plus condensate and has a usual flow rate of 26,417 barrels an hour.
